### R298-001: live macOS alias bypasses bounce's brake

Real macOS tmux was started with `-S /tmp/<owned-scratch>/tmux-<uid>/<label>`.
Accessing that same server with `-L <label>` and its matching `TMUX_TMPDIR`
uses `/private/tmp/<owned-scratch>/tmux-<uid>/<label>`.

The server PID reported by `new-session -P -F '#{pid}'` and by
`display-message -p '#{pid}'` agreed. After stopping only that owned server,
128 queued clients filled its backlog; the next connect returned
`ECONNREFUSED` (61). The bounce setter reported the `/private/tmp/` spelling,
while a successful real `/usr/sbin/lsof -U` still reported `/tmp/`.
Both paths named the same inode.

Executing the exact head's Bash `case` on those observed values selected
`unsafe=""`: bounce would proceed without protecting the live server.
No production daemon was signalled. The owned server was resumed and killed
normally. Compare file identity or consistently resolved paths, retaining a
fail-closed result when identity cannot be established.

### R298-002: parse/stat failure is not proof of absence

Compiled tests using a copy of the exact-head `tmux_sweep.rs`, real macOS
listeners and real absolute-path `lsof` reproduced:

- Live fixture-prefixed sockets with newline, tab and backslash in their names
  were all classified `Stale` and unlinked: `removed: 3`.
- A live socket with an ordinary space in its name was correctly spared.

The output contains escaped pathname representations, but the code passes
them directly to `fs::metadata`. `filter_map(... .ok())` discards the failures
and still returns `Known`, so missing evidence becomes permission to delete.

The Linux branch has the same end result for an ordinary space in
`TMUX_TMPDIR`: `split_whitespace().nth(7)` truncates the pathname after the
seven fixed columns. Replaying the exact Linux parsing expression with the
kernel's unescaped pathname row format and a real live socket under
`with space/` produced `Stale`, `removed: 1`. This is a compiled parser replay
on macOS, not a native Linux runtime claim.

Preserve the complete pathname representation and fail closed for evidence
that cannot safely be mapped to the file. Silently dropping unresolved
holder records is not a valid absence policy.

### R298-003: bound the entire bounce holder acquisition

The new command substitution has no deadline. The actual complete bounce
recipe, with only owned fake build/install/tmux/lsof boundaries, was still
blocked 4,501.84 ms after entering its single holder read; the old scratch
process remained alive. The caller had to terminate its own process group.
This is independent of the earlier setter and post-kill budgets.

Bound the holder read and fail closed on timeout or failed acquisition.
Use the platform's explicit executable path rather than relying on PATH
for this new safety probe. Performance owns the corroborating receipt.

  and unknown holders returned `Stale`, `removed: 1`. This contradicts
  "nothing is removed" on holder failure. No live socket was present in
  this case, so this is a policy/reporting-contract note, not another block.
- The sweep's 10-second budget bounds child polling, not literally every
  possible blocking `wait`/reader `join` at lines 291 and 297-300. No
  normal-use real-lsof descendant/pipe hang was established; this is not
  promoted into another blocker.
- C33's same-user trust boundary is unchanged. The findings concern unsafe
  results from ordinary file identity/representation and acquisition
  handling, not a hostile-seat isolation requirement.

The product audit independently searched daemon/tmux sources for
`ECONNREFUSED`, `ConnectionRefused`, `no server running` and direct Unix
connects. The remaining production `ConnectionRefused` occurrence is TCP
accept-error retry in `daemon/src/serve.rs:90-97`, not absence inference.
Tmux nonzero results become errors (`tmux/src/lib.rs:464-480,526-552`);
reaper/death-sweep, pane observer and pointer worker do not infer absence
from those errors. No additional product refusal-as-gone path was found.

Fixture PID acquisition uses tmux's server `#{pid}`, not the short-lived
client. PID reuse reads as still running and keeps files, so it fails closed.
Candidate symlinks remain excluded; lock opens retain `O_NOFOLLOW`.

Cost: sweep has one macOS lsof per manual run, no per-entry launches;
fixture cleanup polls `kill(pid,0)` every 10 ms for at most 2 s, without
launching per poll; bounce adds one holder launch on refusal only, but its
missing bound is R298-003. No new recurring daemon work.

The sweep's absence evidence is the destructive **policy**; its young-file
check is a one-directional **brake**. Fixture cleanup's policy is server-PID
exit. Bounce's holder check is a **brake** before signalling the daemon.
